segments.speaker: odysseus
segments.caption: Demodocus, above all mortals I honor you — the Muse taught you, surely, or Apollo, for you sing the Achaeans' fate as though you stood among them. Take this cut of honor from my own portion. Now shift your ground and sing the wooden horse, the trap Epeius built with Athena, that noble Odysseus led up into Troy filled with fighting men.

segments.speaker: alcinous
segments.caption: Stop the lyre, Demodocus — not all here take joy of it, for since the song began our guest has not once left off weeping. Now, stranger, hide it no longer: tell me the name your father and mother called you, and your land and your city. And say why you weep at the doom of the Argives and Troy — did some kinsman fall there, or a comrade dear as a brother?
